intro.author: Paul, with Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy named as co-senders (1:1). Traditionally accepted as Paul's; some modern scholars think a follower wrote it in his name.
intro.written: If by Paul, about AD 51, from Corinth, not long after 1 Thessalonians
intro.audience: The church in Thessalonica, still facing persecution
intro.setting: Pressure on the Thessalonian believers had continued. Someone had also unsettled them with the claim that the day of the Lord had already arrived (KJV 'is at hand'), perhaps even by a letter falsely claiming to be from Paul (2:2). Meanwhile some members had stopped working and were living off others (3:6-12).
intro.purpose: Paul encourages the church in suffering, corrects the mistaken claim about the day of the Lord, and instructs them to deal with members who refuse to work.
intro.bigIdea: Stand firm and keep working faithfully, for the Lord's day will come in God's time.

outline.title: The day of the Lord has not yet come

commentary.t: THE SECOND EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS
